issues.title: Row-level execution of small dynamic IN filters behind a selectivity guard
issues.hypothesis: Fresh profile of q02.m0 (8 threads): the supplier TABLE_SCAN is the most expensive operator, at 0.07s cumulative. It emits 96,066 rows with 7 projected columns (FSST s_name/s_phone/s_comment, uncompressed s_address), but only 20,051 survive the next hash join on s_nationkey = n_nationkey, whose build side is 5 nation rows. JoinFilterPushdownInfo::PushInFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:720-759) pushes the 5-key IN list wrapped in a plain OptionalFilter. OptionalFilter::FilterSelection (optional_filter.cpp:23) returns scan_count, so the list is only used for zonemaps and never on rows. The min/max range [min_key, max_key] is pushed as a SelectivityOptionalFilter, but it covers nearly the whole domain and filters nothing. Because no row-level filter is selective, RowGroup::Scan decompresses every string column for all rows. If the IN list ran on rows, the scan would filter s_nationkey first and then use the compression Select path for the remaining columns (FSSTStorage::Select exists, fsst.cpp:791) on about 20% of the rows. That cuts string decode and copy by about 5x, and the s_suppkey join and CTE materialisation would also get pre-filtered input.
issues.plan: 1) In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::PushInFilter (src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp), when in_list.size() <= a small constant (e.g. 16), wrap the InFilter in a SelectivityOptionalFilter instead of OptionalFilter. Use a new threshold constant in selectivity_optional_filter.hpp, e.g. IN_FILTER_THRESHOLD = 0.5f with check_n around 30, so it switches itself off when more than half the rows pass. Larger lists keep the current zonemap-only OptionalFilter. 2) ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp:405) has no IN_FILTER case and would hit the 'unsupported type' InternalException at line 620. Add a case for TableFilterType::IN_FILTER. For integral and other fixed-width physical types, take the IN values into a small typed array once, then loop over the selection keeping rows that are valid and equal to any value (linear scan over k <= 16). Other types fall back to a generic Value-compare loop, or the wrapper is skipped for non-numeric types. Check that TableFilterState::Initialize gives IN_FILTER a usable state; it should be the default state. Alternative if (2) is messy: have the child be an ExpressionFilter over in_filter->ToExpression(BoundReferenceExpression), since EXPRESSION_FILTER is already supported in FilterSelection. Do NOT use ConjunctionOrFilter: its OR merge is quadratic per vector. 3) Check with EXPLAIN ANALYZE that the supplier scan cardinality drops from about 96k to about 20k rows and that results match.
issues.expected_gain: q02: supplier scan 0.07s down to about 0.02-0.03s cumulative, plus less work in the s_suppkey join (0.02s) and the CTE. The supplier branch feeds the CTE on the critical path, so expect roughly 5-10% wall (2-5ms of 45ms).
issues.generality: Any equality join whose build side is a small set of keys (a filtered dimension with at most 16 distinct keys) probing a wider table with payload columns: star and snowflake joins with dimension filters (region/nation/category/date-month style). Queries where the IN list is not selective pay for about 30 vectors of checks, then the guard turns it off. Scans with no extra payload columns gain little. The join already pushes a row-level min/max SelectivityOptionalFilter on the same probe column, so the join types that receive pushed filters are already ones where row-level filtering is safe.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Correctness: the IN list comes only from join keys and excludes NULLs (the ContainsNull check already returns early), so for joins where min/max is already applied on rows, dropping non-matching probe rows earlier is safe. Main risks: a missing IN_FILTER case in some other row-filter path (check that any switch on filter_type reached from the scan handles IN_FILTER, e.g. ColumnData::Filter / FiltersNullValues / ConstantFun::FiltersNullValues), and type mismatch between the in_list values (already cast to the storage type) and the vector's physical type.

dispatch: Row-level execution of small dynamic IN filters behind a selectivity guard
output.memory:
# Memory (planner, specialisation run on q02 = TPC-H Q2 shape, SF10)

## Round 1 findings (gen1)
- q02 baseline ~80ms wall. Plan: part scan (p_size=, suffix LIKE) builds HT -> partsupp scan probes with
  a pushed bloom filter (works: 73k of 8M rows survive, "ps_partkey IN BF"); supplier scan probes a
  tiny nation-region HT, result materialised as CTE __common_subplan; the correlated min() subquery is
  decorrelated via LEFT_DELIM_JOIN + HASH_GROUP_BY over the ~6.5k joined rows (cheap).
- Bloom filter pushdown already exists (JoinFilterPushdownInfo in physical_hash_join.cpp). Don't propose "add BF".
- E0001 ACCEPTED (-18.5%): sub-row-group morsels (RowGroupCollection::GetParallelScanMorselVectors).

## Round 2 (E0002 RETIRED, +2.2% official although the implementer saw -11%)
- E0002 = sparse BitPacking select. No official gain, so payload decode is NOT the bottleneck. Don't retry.
- Measurements are noisy: implementer bench != official bench. q02 hot noise is about ±7%; the bar is -5%.

## Round 3 (E0003 RETIRED: compaction of sparse scan chunks, mean -1.4%, noise)
- Per-chunk overhead after the sparse partsupp BF scan is NOT the bottleneck. Don't retry compaction.
- Profile operator times are cumulative across threads, so they overstate wall gains.

## Round 4
- Current profile (q02.m0, 45ms bench): supplier TABLE_SCAN 0.07s cumulative (largest), 96k rows out,
  only 20k survive the nation join; ps_suppkey=s_suppkey HJ 0.02s; p_partkey HJ 0.01s; CTE 0.01s; delim 0.01s.
- DISPATCHED: row-level execution of small dynamic IN filters (wrap the InFilter in SelectivityOptionalFilter when
  the list has <= 16 values; add an IN_FILTER case to ColumnSegment::FilterSelection). If it fails with no gain,
  string decode of supplier columns is not on the critical path, so look at pipeline/scheduling latency next.
  If it fails on correctness, check the other filter_type switches.

## Codebase facts
- Parallel scan morsel: RowGroupCollection::NextParallelScan (row_group_collection.cpp); now sub-row-group.
- RowGroup::Scan (row_group.cpp:694-824): filters -> col_data.Filter per filter column (adaptive permutation),
  Slice, then col_data.Select for the other columns. Any filter (even optional) forces the partial path.
- StandardColumnData::Select (standard_column_data.cpp:103) falls back to Scan+Slice without compression select.
  FSST has a select (fsst.cpp:791 FSSTStorage::Select); dict_fsst also has one.
- FSST mid-segment start: StartScan delta-decodes the lengths from the segment start (fsst.cpp:615); cheap (<=~12k adds).
- supplier storage at SF10: 1 row group; s_comment FSST 8 segs, s_name/s_phone FSST 3 segs, s_address Uncompressed 12 segs.
- Table filter row execution: ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (column_segment.cpp:405) switch. It handles
  OPTIONAL (delegates), CONJ_OR (quadratic merge!), CONJ_AND, CONSTANT, IS_NULL, STRUCT, BLOOM, EXPRESSION.
  There is NO IN_FILTER case (falls to InternalException).
- OptionalFilter::FilterSelection is a no-op (zonemap only). SelectivityOptionalFilter (subclass) runs its child on rows
  and disables itself above a threshold (MIN_MAX 0.75/30 vectors, BF 0.25/75 vectors).
- Join filter pushdown: JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:814). It pushes min/max as
  SelectivityOptionalFilter, IN (PushInFilter :720) as OptionalFilter, and BF only when not a perfect HT and the build has a filter.
- TableFuncs: TableScanFunc returns each storage.Scan vector directly. HashJoin etc. are CachingPhysicalOperators.
- BitPacking: Skip() loads the next metadata group at an exact group boundary (could read past the end).
- dbe-tool tips: `dbe-tool profile q02.m0 | grep -nE "...|rows|[0-9]\.[0-9][0-9]s" | tr -s ' '` works.
  Avoid braces {n}, awk, sed, head, `grep -v` with regex quirks, and `cd ... ;` compounds (they need approval).
  Use absolute paths in $(cat ...). Profile output is truncated near the partsupp/part scans.
  JSON EXPLAIN output didn't grep well (empty).

## Backlog / directions
- Pipeline/scheduling overhead in q02 (about 10 pipelines incl. CTE + delim join); not investigated yet. Next candidate.
- ps_suppkey = s_suppkey join (0.02s): 32k probes into a 20k HT; would shrink if the supplier side is pre-filtered.
- Supplier scan scaling: an earlier note says 0.05s at 8 threads vs 0.01s at 1 thread, so per-morsel init overhead for 7 columns
  over 12 morsels of a 100k-row table is possible; morsel min size for wide string tables is unexplored.
